slides.title: Beyond Sequential: Complex Architectures 🏛️
slides.content:
# When Sequential Isn't Enough

Sequential chains layers one after another. For skip connections, multiple inputs, or branching, you need a custom `forward()`.

Inherit from `nn.Module`, define layers in `__init__`, and wire them in `forward` with Python logic (if, loops, etc.).

slides.title: Weight Initialization 🎲
slides.content:
## Good Starting Points Matter

Proper weight initialization helps training converge faster. PyTorch defaults to Kaiming/He initialization for linear layers, but you can customize:

```python
def init_weights(m):
    if isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(m.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(m.bias)

model.apply(init_weights)
```

slides.title: Custom Initialization
slides.content: Apply Xavier initialization to all linear layers.
slides.codeSnippet:
model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4,10), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(10,3))

def init_weights(m):
    if isinstance(m, nn.Linear):
        nn.init.xavier_uniform_(m.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(m.bias, 0.01)

model.apply(init_weights)
print(model[0].weight.mean(), model[0].weight.std())

slides.title: Common Init Schemes 📚
slides.content:
## torch.nn.init functions

* `xavier_uniform_`, `xavier_normal_` – good for tanh/sigmoid.
* `kaiming_uniform_`, `kaiming_normal_` – designed for ReLU.
* `uniform_`, `normal_` – generic.
* `constant_`, `zeros_`, `ones_` – for biases.

Always use **in‑place** versions (with `_`) to modify existing tensors.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Lazy Initialization with `nn.LazyLinear`

If you don't know the input size upfront, use `nn.LazyLinear(out_features)`. It infers `in_features` on the first forward pass.
